_comment: Source registry. Every candidate must trace to one of these, and `allowlist`
is what the primary-source rule is actually checked against (src/verify.js).
`enabled: true` means the adapter was run against the live endpoint and it
returned real items. Entries with `enabled: false` are ones I want but could
not confirm — the probe result is recorded in `note` so nobody re-discovers
it. Turn one on only once its adapter genuinely works; a source that 404s
silently is worse than one that is honestly switched off.

sources.name: UK FCDO — Foreign travel advice
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200, 13KB, items present. Each entry is a country page whose 'latest update' line states what changed — the best single feed for entry and visa changes. dedupeBy url+updated added 2026-09-14: this is a rolling feed of just-revised advisories at permanent per-country URLs, so URL-derived identity made the first sighting of each country the only one for SEEN_TTL_DAYS and silently dropped every later revision.

sources.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — news
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200, 9KB, items present. New inscriptions and site decisions — strong for place and hidden-spot posts.

sources.name: JNTO — Japan National Tourism Organization
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200, 17KB, items present. Japanese-language titles; the drafting step translates, and verify.js still requires the claim to trace to this page. urlIncludes added 2026-09-14: the feed also carries JNTO's corporate wire (procurement notices, trade-show exhibitor recruitment, B2B seminars) — 14 of 15 items on the day it was measured, all of them stub pages of 178-419 chars against a 700 floor. /news/press/ is the travel news.

sources.name: NASA Earth Observatory
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-23: 200, 10 items, article pages ~10k chars. NASA writing about one specific place on Earth per day, from orbit - the closest thing to a surprising-fact source that is still primary.

sources.name: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program — weekly report
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-23: 200, 29KB. Weekly eruption and unrest reports - Etna, Asosan and the rest. Travel-relevant and inherently interesting, and the standing global authority on the question. Every item links to the same weekly landing page, so identity is taken from the title.

sources.name: Open-Meteo Climate API (ERA5)
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200, valid JSON. Not a feed — a queryable dataset. The adapter asks it about destinations in data/destinations.json and proposes when-to-go candidates from real monthly normals.

sources.name: This is Athens — the official Athens guide
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 126KB, 10 items with ~1,500-char summaries, article pages ~1,800 chars. Events and 'what's new' for the city Israelis fly to most - a three-year closure of the Odeon of Herodes Atticus, a car-free day. Links are http:// and redirect to https on the same host.

sources.name: Kyoto City Tourism Association
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 17KB, 50 items, English, no summaries but article pages ~6,000 chars. Festival viewing seats, guided tours, tax and currency rules, seasonal dance performances - the practical, dated things a visitor to Kyoto actually books.

sources.name: JNTO — Travel Japan blog
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 6KB, 10 items spread over a year, article pages ~12,000 chars. JNTO's English long-form: national parks, heritage villages, museums. Slow, but every item is a place with a way to get there.

sources.name: Vietnam National Authority of Tourism
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 76KB, 10 items with full 1,500-char summaries, pages ~2,000+ chars. Islands, street food, heritage villages. One stale 2021 item sits in the feed and recency handles it. Needed the parser's entity budget lifted (src/sources/rss.js).

sources.name: Tourism Authority of Thailand — newsroom
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 14KB, 10 items, pages ~6,000 chars. Roughly half is trade - MoUs, travel marts, the Governor welcoming a minister - and the scorer's trade-noise penalty was extended for exactly that vocabulary. The other half is Bangkok events, heritage walks and festival dates for the most-flown long-haul destination.

sources.name: My Helsinki — the city's official guide
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 200KB, 10 items, pages ~6,000 chars. Neighbourhood guides and seven-things lists, all with addresses. A small destination for Israelis, so it will mostly lose on ranking - but it never produces noise.

sources.name: Sydney.com — Destination NSW
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 7KB, 10 items, pages ~12,000 chars. Ocean pools, markets, a day trip to the Royal National Park - long, specific and photographable. Links carry utm_ parameters, which candidateId() already strips.

sources.name: US Dept of State — Travel Advisories
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200 and well-formed, but the channel contains ZERO items — it is an empty shell. Left off until a feed with actual entries is found.

sources.name: Israel NSC / MFA — travel warnings
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: gov.il sits behind Imperva and returns 403 to any non-browser client. Needs a real browser fetch (we already ship Playwright) before it can be enabled.

sources.name: Israel Airports Authority — news
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 404 at every obvious RSS path, and the site is behind the same Imperva stack as gov.il. Primary source for TLV routes, so worth the scraper eventually.

sources.name: EU — Entry/Exit System & ETIAS
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200 but client-rendered HTML with no feed. Directly relevant to Israeli travellers to Schengen; needs a Playwright-backed extractor.

sources.name: Ryanair — newsroom
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: connection refused to non-browser clients (curl got 000).

sources.name: Wizz Air — media & news
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 404 at the documented path. Needs the current URL confirmed.

sources.name: Aegean Airlines — press office
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 403 Access Denied to non-browser clients.

sources.name: ESA — Observing the Earth
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 15 items - but it is mission news (launches, contracts, briefings), not the 'Earth from Space' place-of-the-week series, and no separate feed for that series was found at any obvious path. Left off: NASA Earth Observatory already covers this and covers it better.

sources.name: US National Park Service — Grand Canyon news
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 225 items, pages ~3,500 chars. The per-park feed pattern works for every park code (yell, yose, zion...). Left off because the feed is mostly administration and grief - fatalities, flood recovery, superintendent appointments - and even with the grim-title filter the useful fraction (timed entry, road openings) is thin. Turn on a park in the season it matters, with its own id.

sources.name: Visit València — agenda
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 25 items in five days, Spanish, pages ~2,600 chars. An events agenda: World Paella Day and a Moros y Cristianos parade beside a dozen arena concerts. Usable once the scorer can tell a festival from a concert listing; until then it would spend draft budget on Servando y Florentino.

sources.name: visitBerlin — blog
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items - but the /en/ feed links to /de/ articles, and half the items are 2018 posts re-dated on edit. German-language pages the model can read, and a good source for Berlin, once an English feed or a stable date is found.

sources.name: Visit Maldives — experiences
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items, pages ~2,700 chars. The /news feed is all MoUs and award ceremonies; this one is resort marketing written by the resorts. Neither is a fact a reader can act on. Off until the DMO publishes something about the islands rather than the hotels.

sources.name: Visit Cyprus — Deputy Ministry of Tourism
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items - directory entries (a restaurant name, a luna park, a PDF map) with 50-200 char summaries and pages under the thin floor. The one real item, a mountain village page, was 1,668 chars. Off until the feed carries articles.

sources.name: The Royal Parks — London
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items - three seasonal walks (Regent's Park, Hyde Park, Richmond) and seven FAQ entries. The walk links 404 at the URL the feed gives, so nothing can be fetched and verified. Worth re-probing: an autumn walk in Richmond Park is exactly the post this channel wants.
